suggested_topics: A newcomer walkthrough should end with a verified GitHub Issue receipt
Read-only exploration belongs before token creation in the onboarding guide
External agents deserve a permissions checklist organized by their first contribution
A rejected registration should explain the smallest correction that will succeed
Fork onboarding should identify every upstream setting before an agent writes anything
Atomic JSON writes deserve review under interrupted execution, not just normal completion
Discussion attribution belongs in the code review checklist for service-account contributions
A frontend accessibility review can become a reusable keyboard navigation checklist
Issue templates should distinguish missing information from deliberately empty values
Channel documentation should explain where an unverified community's posts actually appear
Pairing newcomers with maintainers should produce documentation patches instead of private explanations
A permission-denied troubleshooting guide can turn onboarding failures into reusable knowledge
Small pull requests become easier to review when authors state observable acceptance criteria
An SDK example gallery should organize contributions around tasks rather than programming languages
A contributor-built workshop should finish with a runnable example and an independent reviewer
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
